promises.text: 2012 campaign: Why running: "We need leaders more concerned about creating jobs than protecting their own."
2012 campaign: Priority on taxes: said it is imperative to stimulate the local economy by reducing taxes on citizens and businesses; said the Penny for Pasco sales tax distributes the burden equally
2012 campaign: Priority on county leadership: called for a nationwide search for a new county administrator with experience in a county of 750,000 to 1,000,000 people
2012 campaign: Priority on mobility fees: said he did not understand replacing impact fees with mobility fees, which he said do not cover the entire cost of infrastructure
2016 campaign: Said the mobility fee formula should change so rural and urban areas pay the same rate; said he did not favor increasing school impact fees
2016 campaign: When filing for the 2016 race, named flooding, redevelopment and transportation as top issues facing the county

votes.officialTitle: Zoning Amendment (Regular) - Chanzep LLC - Chanzep MPUD Master Planned Unit Development - A Rezoning Petition Request From an A-R Agricultural Residential District to an MPUD Master Planned Unit Development District to Allow for the Development of 96 Platted Townhome Units and Associated Infrastructure - Southeast Pasco County - Located South of Chancey Road Approximately 777 Feet East of the Chancey Road and Gall Boulevard Intersection - Containing Approximately 20.42 Acres
votes.minutesText: Approved Staff's recommendation with Chairman Mariano voting nay.

does.text: Rezones about 20.42 acres of mostly vacant land south of Chancey Road, east of Gall Boulevard in southeast Pasco, from agricultural-residential to a master planned unit development that allows up to 96 townhomes, about 4.7 homes per acre. The owner, Chanzep LLC, must follow staff's conditions, including landscape buffers along Crystal Springs Road and Chancey Road, a 5-foot sidewalk extension on Crystal Springs Road and a 10-foot multi-use path along Chancey Road. The off-site part of that walking and biking work can be credited against the bike and pedestrian share of the project's mobility fees.

votes.headline: Approved the Two Rivers expansion and a path for a surf park
votes.inShort: Commissioners approved a land use change and rezoning (items P47 and P56) that expand the Two Rivers community in Wesley Chapel and clear the way for a proposed 35-acre surf park. The change adds 900 multifamily homes, of which no more than 240 can be garden-style apartments.

does.text: Expands what can be built in the 3,405-acre Two Rivers development along State Road 56 between Morris Bridge Road and Gall Boulevard in Wesley Chapel. The apartment limit rises from 1,600 to 2,500 units, retail space roughly doubles to about 1.3 million square feet, up to 480 hotel rooms, a 300-bed assisted living facility and one water park of up to 35 acres are added, 209 age-restricted homes are dropped, and the 4,047 single-family homes already allowed stay the same; the board also adopted a matching change to the county's comprehensive plan for Two Rivers. Of the 900 added multifamily homes, no more than 240 may be apartments; the rest must be condos, townhomes, duplexes, villas or similar, per the staff memo. The board changed the condition tying the apartments to the water park at the hearing; Wesley Chapel Community reported the final rule as: the apartments cannot break ground until the surf park gets its certificate of occupancy or three years pass, whichever comes first.

votes.headline: Moved $2 million from county reserves to a New Port Richey septic-to-sewer project
votes.inShort: Transferred $2,000,000 from the county's general fund reserves to the City of New Port Richey to help pay for connecting the Town and Country Villas neighborhood from septic tanks to sewer.
votes.officialTitle: Budget Amendment — Transfer from the Board General Fund Reserves — City of New Port Richey — Funding for Town and Country Villas Septic to Sewer Project — $2,000,000.00
votes.minutesText: Approved Staff's recommendation with Chairman Mariano voting nay.

does.text: Moves $2,000,000 from the county's General Fund reserves and pays it to the City of New Port Richey for the Town and Country Villas neighborhood, where the city plans to replace septic tanks with a sanitary sewer system. The payment carries out a Dec 5, 2023 agreement in which the county pledged $2 million for water and sewer work and the city pledged at least $1.5 million for roads, stormwater, trees and streetlights; the county had budgeted the money in FY 2023, but the agreement terms were not met that year and it was never paid. The city asked for the money after its application for a state Water Quality Improvement Grant for the sewer system was not selected.

votes.headline: Approved $156.2 million in federal disaster recovery money for storm projects
votes.inShort: The board approved $156,162,158.85 in federal disaster recovery (CDBG-DR) money for the first phase of its storm repair and mitigation program after Hurricanes Idalia, Helene and Milton: 22 projects plus $1 million for the county's share of FEMA projects (item R43).

does.text: Approves Phase 1 of Pasco's Better Future Infrastructure and Mitigation Program: 22 projects totaling $155,162,158.85 plus $1,000,000 for the local share of future FEMA repair projects, for $156,162,158.85 in all, paid with federal Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) money for recovery from Hurricanes Idalia, Helene and Milton. Projects include Sea Pines flood abatement in Hudson (about $28.9 million across two line items), Double Hammock Creek flood abatement ($23.9 million), Mitchell Boulevard ($15 million), Elfers septic-to-sewer ($10 million), a Dade City recreation, veterans center and shelter ($12 million) and the Hudson Library renovation. Each project still needs final eligibility, environmental and duplication-of-benefits reviews, procurement and signed agreements before money is committed or construction starts; Bay News 9 reported that projects must be finished within five years or the county may have to repay funds.

after.text: On the consent agenda, the board approved Better Future public services policies and procedures covering $10,000,000 in CDBG-DR funds (item C40, ODRR26-0026).
On the consent agenda, the board approved a budget amendment for Phase 1 Better Future planning projects funded with $7,404,010.20 in CDBG-DR money (item C24, ODRR27-0002).

votes.headline: Rezoned a 2.3-acre corner at Little Road and DeCubellis Road for commercial use
votes.inShort: Changed the zoning on about 2.3 acres at the northeast corner of Little Road and DeCubellis Road in west Pasco to general commercial, after removing language about DeCubellis Road from the approval.
votes.officialTitle: Zoning Amendment (Consent) – 7026 Little Road/Roosevelt Commons, L.L.C. – Change in Zoning from an R-4 High Density Residential District, C-1 Neighborhood Commercial District, and A-C Agricultural District to a C-2 General Commercial District – West Pasco County – Northeast Corner of the Intersection of Little Road and Decubellis Road – Containing Approximately 2.3 Acres
votes.minutesText: Approved Staff's recommendation with the revision to remove the DeCubellis Road language entirely by roll call vote with Commissioner Yeager voting nay.

does.text: Rezones about 2.3 acres at the northeast corner of Little Road and DeCubellis Road in west Pasco (7026 Little Road and 8531 DeCubellis Road) to C-2 general commercial, so the site can be developed for businesses. Deed restrictions proposed by staff bar uses such as stand-alone car washes, self-storage, auto repair, used-car sales and towing yards. Staff's draft also barred a gas station until the county widens DeCubellis Road to four lanes (project CIP 20032) or a gas station on an opposite corner closes; the minutes say the board removed the DeCubellis Road language entirely but do not quote the wording removed.

votes.headline: Renewal of the Sheriff's license-plate camera agreement failed on a 2 to 2 tie
votes.inShort: Commissioner Yeager moved to renew the county's agreement letting the Sheriff's Office run license-plate cameras on county roads. The motion failed 2 to 2, with Commissioner Weightman absent. A tie means a motion fails.

does.text: The motion to keep the county's agreement letting the Pasco Sheriff's Office run license-plate reader cameras on county rights-of-way failed on a 2 to 2 tie: Commissioner Yeager, who made the motion, and Commissioner Starkey voted yes; Commissioner Oakley and Chairman Mariano voted no; Commissioner Weightman was absent. A tie means a motion fails. Because it failed, the renewal was not approved that day; Tampa Bay Beacons reported that the new contract would have switched camera vendors from Flock to Axon. The county agreement covered about 60 cameras in county rights-of-way, while about 110 cameras owned by homeowners associations, stores and other private owners were not part of it, per Tampa Bay Beacons.

after.text: Commissioners discussed a possible committee, a workshop and a task force on license-plate readers. Tampa Bay Beacons reported that the board directed staff to form a task force of residents and experts to study the cameras, drones and related technology, with a public workshop expected before any future program.

Tampa Bay Beacons reported that, the day after the Aug 25 meeting, Sheriff Chris Nocco sent a letter ending the agreement effective Sept 30. Nocco blamed commissioners who no longer supported it and warned that losing the cameras would hurt efforts to solve crimes and find missing people.

votes.headline: Approved pilot programs for school zone speed cameras and safety systems
votes.inShort: Approved two pilot programs: school zone speed detection cameras and the IntelliRoad School Zone Safety System. The item said no county funding was required. The minutes note the Sheriff's deputies will patrol schools as much as they can until the programs start.
votes.officialTitle: Discussion on School Zone Speed Detection Systems (SDS) and IntelliRoad School Zone Safety System (SZSS) Pilot Program – No Funding Required
votes.minutesText: Approved to adopt both programs as per the Sheriff they patrol the schools as much as they can until the program is implemented with Chairman Mariano voting nay.

does.text: Tells county staff to pursue an ordinance allowing school zone speed cameras, and to take part in a no-cost pilot of IntelliRoad's AI-based School Zone Safety System at one school crosswalk. A 2023 state law (HB 657) lets counties ticket drivers going more than 10 mph over a school zone limit. Staff said a Pasco camera program would first need an ordinance, agreements with the Sheriff's Office, New Port Richey and Zephyrhills, a countywide awareness campaign, a vendor and installation, and that ticket money would be split as state law requires among the county, the School District, the state and a crossing guard program. The pilot uses detection cameras, flashing beacons and audio alerts to warn drivers, and staff said this step needs no additional county money.

votes.headline: Put a one-year pause on new data centers
votes.inShort: The county froze permits, rezonings and site plans for new data centers in unincorporated Pasco for 12 months while it works out how to regulate them.

does.text: For 12 months, Pasco County will not accept applications for building permits, site plans, rezonings, comprehensive plan changes or other approvals for data centers and other 'large load' electricity users in unincorporated Pasco. Server or computer rooms that support a site's main use and draw no more than 2.5 megawatts are exempt, and the board can still approve a development agreement for a data center that is not a large load customer if it sets conditions on location, size, water use, power use, noise, electronic waste and other impacts. Tampa Bay Beacons reported that the moratorium is retroactive to May 27, and that planning director David Engel said a proposed data center at Double Branch cannot proceed under it; the pause can end early if the county adopts permanent rules, or the board can extend it by resolution.
